messages.author: f036ee166979266c
messages.subject: using google's causalImpact with renjin
parts:
Hi, 

I'm trying to expose google's causalImpact library through a web API (https://github.com/google/CausalImpact) and renjin seems to be the way to achieve my goals.
Problem is, it seems that devtools is not quite supported yet (http://packages.renjin.org/packages/devtools.html).

I'm quite new to R, I'm wondering if I can load causalImpact R files directly into renjin.
Also, if you guys have any advice on how to expose some R stats through a HTTP api that would be great. CausalImpact doesn't seem to have many knobs, so I'm guessing it's just a matter of supplying the dataset and chewing it.

Thanks,
Miguel

messages.author: 3b104dc6686d0c85
messages.subject: Re: using google's causalImpact with renjin
parts:
Hi Miguel,

You only use devtools if you want to install a package from GitHub into GNU R. Renjin uses a different packaging mechanism so devtools cannot be used, even if you could run it in Renjin.

The package you are referring to will not work due to some of its dependencies that are not available in Renjin, such as dplyr and ggplot2.

Your only option would be to follow the instructions at http://docs.renjin.org to create a package for Renjin with only the core functions from the Google package while avoiding the use of dplyr and others. But that is probably quite a big task, especially if you're new to R.

Sorry we can't help you any more with this.

Maarten-Jan
